messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: PD#INC-2026 - service-discovery.srv.lookup.errors > 30% in us-east-1a. Affected SRV: _core._tcp.internal. Notifying oncall.
Olivia (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Seeing spike in 5xx on model-router from service discovery failures.
Olivia (oncall): quick check - are there any recent infra deploys in us-east-1a?
Ravi (infra): no deploys in last hour. We just had a minor control-plane upgrade yesterday but that was global.
Maya (network): checking peering/fabric for east1a. QPS to coredns from that AZ is ~3x normal.
Chen (sre): grabbing logs from coredns pods now.
Chen (sre): log snippet: ```2026-03-15T14:07:12Z error lookup _core._tcp.internal: net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded)```
Olivia (oncall): thanks. Could be DNS forwarders saturating. Can someone run a quick SRV query against the coredns instance in east1a and a healthy east1b?
Ravi (infra): running: ```dig +short SRV _core._tcp.internal @10.2.14.6``` -> returns truncated / no answer intermittently.
Maya (network): I see increased TCP retransmits between east1a nodes and our DNS-egress gateway. Packet drops on the peer link for AZ-a. Tie-in with cloud provider ticket? Opening with provider now.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026. Severity: Sev2. Conference bridge: #call-INC-2026.
Olivia (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) split traffic to east1b for service discovery using regional routing policy 2) scale up coredns replicas in east1a to absorb retry storms 3) temporary workaround: increase SRV lookup TTL on consul services to reduce QPS. Applying now.
Ravi (infra): scaling coredns replicas: ```kubectl scale deploy coredns -n kube-system --replicas=6 --context=us-east-1a``` -> command accepted.
Chen (sre): bumping consul TTLs for core services: ```consul services register -name=model-router -port=8080 -check=... -ttl=60s``` -> increasing to 300s. Pushed for model-router and shard-proxy.
Maya (network): routing change applied: added policy to route DNS from east1a to east1b resolver pool for SRV queries: ```route-policy add --match srv --src az=us-east-1a --target resolver-pool-east1b```
Olivia (oncall): monitoring metrics... error-rate dropping to ~12% after routing change. Latency for SRV lookups in impacted services reduced from 400ms->120ms.
Support Bot: noticed customer errors spike for org 'faststream' - 37% failed requests in past 10m.
Nate (product): flagging customers with SLO exposure. Which customers hit SLOs?
Olivia (oncall): initial list: faststream, analytics-inc, campus-ai. Support/CS to reach out if needed.
Ravi (infra): there are still intermittent timeouts when queries hit local coredns, but cross-az routing keeps things online. Suggest keeping reroute for 1 hour while provider investigates.
Maya (network): provider acknowledged suspected peering micro-outage in us-east-1a. They've routed around but advise we keep traffic off the affected fabric for 30-60m.
Chen (sre): creating a short-term runbook note: "If SRV errors > 20% in an AZ, switch regional resolver to neighbor AZ and increase TTLs; scale coredns to 6; notify provider".
Olivia (oncall): will handoff to night oncall in 45m. Leaving notes on the conference bridge.
incident-bot: oncall handoff scheduled for 2026-03-15T15:00:00Z to Ravi (oncall-weekend).
Ravi (infra): taking handoff early. I'll keep monitoring DNS QPS and consul health checks.
Nate (product): nui: set external comms? We should prepare a short status for impacted customers saying partial service degradation in us-east-1a; mitigation in place and most traffic routed.
Support Bot: drafting message for faststream and analytics-inc: "We've detected service discovery errors impacting some requests originating in us-east-1a. Mitigations applied which have reduced errors; engineering is monitoring. We'll update in 1h."
Olivia (oncall): thanks everyone. Postmortem owner: Chen. Please collect coredns logs, network packet counters, and consul health history for writeup.
Chen (sre): ack. Will include exact command outputs: ```kubectl logs -n kube-system deploy/coredns --since=30m | grep lookup | tail -n 200``` and tcpdump snippets from affected nodes.
Maya (network): I'll include provider ticket ID: PGP-78911 and the peering trace.
Olivia (oncall): closing the immediate pager; keeping the incident channel open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert resolved: PD#INC-2026 - all checks green in monitoring.
